mainTopic: "זה בני" and the reasoning of הואיל: how far a husband is believed about divorcing his wife, and whether a statement can be split
overview: The משנה taught that a man who says "זה בני" (this is my son) is believed. The גמרא explains that the new point is freeing his wife from יבום, even when he is known to have a brother. שמואל's reason, in its corrected form, is הואיל: he is believed because he has the power to divorce her now. רב יוסף uses this to say that a husband who says "I divorced my wife" is believed. A report from רבי יוחנן seems to reject that, but another report of רבי יוחנן says he is believed. The גמרא settles it: he is not believed about the past (למפרע), but he is believed about the future (להבא). רב מארי and רב זביד then argue whether a past claim can at least count from now on, which is the question of splitting a statement (פלגינן דיבורא). The view that we do not split is defended against רבא's adultery ruling. We split a statement between two people, but not about one person.

steps.title: Being believed about inheritance is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say a man is believed about who inherits him. That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That he is believed for this son to inherit him is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that "זה בני" is believed. As far as ירושה goes, why would we need to be told?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may give his property to anyone he likes as a gift. So if he points to someone and says "this is my son," of course that person can take his property. A rule that teaches nothing new needs an explanation.

phrases.english: Regarding inheriting him, it is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of the משנה's ruling of "זה בני נאמן".
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to say that "זה בני" is believed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He could give this person his property as a gift anyway, so being believed for ירושה adds nothing new.

steps.title: The real point is freeing his wife from levirate marriage
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed to teach that he is believed to free his wife from יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed to free his wife from יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's new teaching is not about ירושה. It is that his word frees his wife from יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man cannot simply decide that his wife will be free from יבום. That depends on whether he leaves children. Even so, the משנה says his claim of having a son is accepted for this, and that is the new point.

keyTerms.meaning: levirate marriage: a childless man's widow marries his brother

phrases.english: To exempt his wife from levirate marriage
it was necessary for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִפְטוֹר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִן הַיִּבּוּם אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the new teaching to a different area of law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be teaching only about ירושה, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that he is believed to free his wife from יבום, which is not in his power to do.

steps.title: A משנה already taught this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that a משנה in קידושין already says a dying man who claims to have children is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this too: one who said as he was dying, "I have children," is believed. If he said "I have brothers," he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 2. Freeing the wife from יבום through his word was already taught in another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in קידושין says a dying man is believed when he says "I have children," so his wife is free from יבום. He is not believed when he says "I have brothers," which would tie her to יבום. If so, our משנה seems to repeat something already known.

keyTerms.meaning: at the time of his death

phrases.english: We already learned this as well:
One who said at the time of his death:
"I have children" is believed.
"I have brothers" is not believed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 2 by showing it repeats an earlier משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that freeing the wife from יבום is what the משנה adds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in קידושין already teaches that his claim of having children frees his wife from יבום, so our משנה would be repeating it.

steps.title: Our משנה adds the case where he is known to have a brother
steps.stepSummary: In קידושין he was not known to have a brother. Our משנה teaches he is believed even when he is known to have one.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he is not known to us to have a brother. Here, he is believed even though he is known to have a brother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by showing the two משניות deal with different cases. Ours teaches something the other did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קידושין, no brother is known, so his wife is free from יבום in any case, and his words only back that up. Our משנה teaches that even when a brother is known, which would normally require יבום, his claim of having a son still frees her. That is a real new point.

keyTerms.meaning: known, presumed to be the case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two משניות argue. Each one deals with a different situation: no known brother there, a known brother here.
steps.whatToRemember: "זה בני נאמן" teaches that a man's word frees his wife from יבום even when he is known to have a brother.

phrases.english: There, he is not presumed by us to have a brother,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא – אַף עַל גַּב דְּמוּחְזָק לֵיהּ בְּאָח.
phrases.english: Here, even though he is presumed to have a brother.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Tells the two cases apart (אוקימתא of the situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה seemed to repeat the משנה in קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה adds that he is believed even when he is known to have a brother.

steps.title: Why he is believed: a husband who says he divorced is believed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that "זה בני" is believed because a husband who says "I divorced my wife" is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה, in the name of שמואל: Why did they say that "this is my son" is believed? Because a husband who said "I divorced my wife" is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the reason a man is believed to free his wife from יבום by saying "this is my son." He compares it to a husband who says he divorced her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband who says "I divorced my wife" is believed, and a divorced woman has no יבום. Since he could free her that way, he is also believed when he frees her by saying he has a son. The question form here only opens the explanation; it does not challenge anything.

keyTerms.meaning: for what reason did they say

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why a man has the power to free his wife from יבום even though that normally depends on facts beyond his control.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
For what reason did they say:
"This is my son" is believed?
Since a husband who said:
"I divorced my wife" is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting what the משנה teaches, it now explains the reason behind the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "זה בני" is believed to free the wife from יבום because the husband could free her anyway by saying "I divorced my wife," which is believed.

steps.title: רב יוסף objects: a משנה cannot depend on a rule not taught in a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף is shocked by the reasoning in step 5. It explains a rule that is taught in the משנה ("זה בני") using a rule that is not taught in any משנה (a husband who says "I divorced my wife").
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Master of Abraham! Should we hang something that is taught in a משנה on something that is not taught?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the explanation from step 5. He says it builds a clear משנה on top of a rule that is not found in any משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, "זה בני" was believed BECAUSE a husband who says "I divorced my wife" is believed. But "זה בני" is written in our משנה, while the divorce-claim rule is only a later statement. You cannot explain a solid source by leaning on a weaker one, so the reasoning must be wrong or misquoted.

keyTerms.meaning: "Master of Abraham!", a cry of shock that calls on ה׳
that which is not taught in a משנה

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Master of Abraham!
phrases.notes: A cry of amazement, like saying "Oh my God!" He can't believe this reasoning.

phrases.english: Shall we hang what is taught on what is not taught?!
phrases.notes: "What is taught" is "זה בני" in our משנה. "What is not taught" is the husband who says "I divorced my wife."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning given in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reasoning (as reported in step 5) that "זה בני" is believed because a husband who says "I divorced my wife" is believed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule taught in a משנה cannot be grounded in a rule that is not taught in any משנה.

steps.title: Corrected version of שמואל: he is believed since he has the power to divorce her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates שמואל's words. "זה בני" is believed because the husband could divorce his wife right now, and that would also free her from יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, this is how it was said. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Why did they say that "זה בני" is believed? Since it is in his power to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the quote from שמואל so that it no longer leans on an outside rule. The new reason is that the husband has the power to divorce her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the reason borrowed a separate הלכה about claiming a past divorce. Now the reason is a simple fact: the husband could give a גט today, and that would free her from יבום anyway. Since he could reach the same result by acting, he is believed when he reaches it by speaking ("this is my son").

keyTerms.meaning: if it was said, this is how it was said, a formula that corrects a quote
since: a claim is believed because the person could do the same thing in another way
it is in his power to divorce her

steps.confusionAlert: "הואיל ובידו לגרשה" does NOT mean he actually divorced her. It means he COULD divorce her now, so his words are trusted for the same result.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the famous principle of הואיל ("since he could have"), which the rest of this piece tests.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said,
this is how it was said:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
For what reason did they say
that "This is my son" is believed?
phrases.notes: Believed for freeing his wife from יבום, as explained in step 2.

phrases.english: Since it is in his power to divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's objection by restating שמואל's reason
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrected version of the quote (אי אתמר הכי אתמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reason relied on the rule of a husband who claims he divorced
steps.terutzMaskana: The reason is that he has the power to divorce her now (הואיל)

steps.title: רב יוסף: a husband who says 'I divorced my wife' is believed too
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף builds on the הואיל idea. A husband who claims "I divorced my wife" should also be believed, since he could divorce her right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Now that you say we use "הואיל", a husband who says "I divorced my wife" is believed, since it is in his power to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף takes the new reason from step 7 and applies it to another case. He rules that a husband's claim of a past divorce is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband's power to divorce now makes "זה בני" believable, the same power should make "I already divorced her" believable. Notice the reversal: before, the divorce claim was the source, and now it is a result of הואיל. This new ruling is what the next step will test.

keyTerms.meaning: we say, we apply this reasoning

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Now that you have said that we say "since,"
a husband who said, "I divorced my wife"
is believed,
since it is in his power to divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the הואיל principle from step 7 to a new case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who says "I divorced my wife" is believed, because of הואיל ובידו לגרשה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a husband who says 'I divorced my wife' is not believed
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף brings a ruling of רבי יוחנן that says the opposite of רב יוסף: such a husband is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: A husband who says "I divorced my wife" is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: A teaching from ארץ ישראל arrives that directly contradicts רב יוסף's ruling from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the husband IS believed. In this report, רבי יוחנן says he is NOT. That seems to knock down רב יוסף's use of הואיל for this case. Step 12 shows this ruling applies only to a claim about the past.

keyTerms.meaning: when he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: When Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
a husband who said, "I divorced my wife"
is not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts רב יוסף's ruling in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's ruling that a husband who claims he divorced is believed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן rules the opposite, so the הואיל reasoning cannot be applied to this case

steps.title: רב ששת: רב יוסף's 'since' is gone
steps.stepSummary: רב שֵׁשֶׁת waves his hand to dismiss רב יוסף's ruling. רבי יוחנן's statement knocks it down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שֵׁשֶׁת waved his hand: רב יוסף's "הואיל" is gone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שֵׁשֶׁת draws the conclusion. Because of רבי יוחנן, רב יוסף's use of הואיל for the divorce claim no longer stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hand-wave shows a decisive rejection. What falls is רב יוסף's extension to a husband who claims a past divorce, which was the idea in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: waved his hand, a gesture of dismissal
it is gone, it has fallen

steps.whatToRemember: "זה בני" is believed to free the wife from יבום, הואיל ובידו לגרשה (since he could divorce her now). רב ששת thinks רבי יוחנן's ruling knocks out רב יוסף's extension to a husband who says "I divorced my wife." The next two steps show this is not the final word: such a husband is believed about the future (להבא) but not about the past (למפרע).

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet waved his hand:
phrases.notes: A gesture of brushing something away, as if to say "that's finished."

phrases.english: Rav Yosef's "since" is gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנַפַּח רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בִּידֵיהּ אֲזַל לֵיהּ הוֹאִיל דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב ששת, רב יוסף's ruling based on הואיל, that a husband who claims he divorced is believed, is rejected. Steps 11-12 then limit this: he is not believed למפרע, but he is believed להבא.

steps.title: A different report of רבי יוחנן says the husband is believed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling from step 9. רבי חייא בר אבין reports that רבי יוחנן said a husband who claims "I divorced my wife" IS believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a husband who says "I divorced my wife" is believed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוחנן really said the husband is not believed. It brings another quote from רבי יוחנן that says the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, רב יצחק בר יוסף quoted רבי יוחנן: the husband is NOT believed. Now רבי חייא בר אבין quotes רבי יוחנן: the husband IS believed. The same חכם can't hold both views about the same case, so something must be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is that so?" An opening that challenges a statement just made
"But doesn't..." Brings a source that contradicts what was just said

phrases.english: Is that so?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is questioning the ruling quoted in step 9 in the name of רבי יוחנן, that the husband is not believed.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A husband who says "I divorced my wife" is believed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבי יוחנן ruling that was used in steps 9-10 to reject רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report from step 9 that רבי יוחנן holds a husband claiming "I divorced my wife" is not believed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between two reports of the same חכם: another student quotes רבי יוחנן as saying the husband IS believed.

steps.title: About the past he is not believed, about the future he is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both quotes are true, but they cover different cases. When the husband claims he divorced her at an earlier time (למפרע), he is not believed. When his claim only matters from now on (להבא), he is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. Here (where he is not believed) it is about the past. There (where he is believed) it is about the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases: one ruling is about the past, the other is about the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband has the power to divorce his wife right now, so his claim is believed for the future, using the same הואיל idea from step 7. But he has no power to divorce her in the past. So if he says she was already divorced on an earlier date, which would change how we judge what she did back then, he is not believed.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is not difficult." The usual opening of an answer that removes a contradiction
"Here... there." Each ruling applies to a different case
Backward in time; about the past
From now on; about the future

steps.whatToRemember: A husband's claim "I divorced my wife" is believed only where he could do it now, meaning for the future. He is not believed to change the past.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two "כָּאן"s. The first (למפרע) matches the ruling that he is NOT believed, from step 9. The second (להבא) matches the ruling that he IS believed, from step 11.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit of the הואיל reasoning: "since he could do it now" works only for what he could actually do now. It sets up the next question.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
here it is about the past,
phrases.notes: This means he claims the divorce already happened at some earlier date. Here he is not believed, since he can't divorce her in the past.

phrases.english: there it is about the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן לְמַפְרֵעַ כָּאן לְהַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ruling of רבי יוחנן applies to a different time frame.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like רבי יוחנן contradicted himself about whether the husband is believed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not believed about the past (למפרע); believed about the future (להבא), since he could divorce her now.

steps.title: If he claimed a past divorce, is he believed at least from now on?
steps.stepSummary: A new question is raised. If the husband said he divorced her at an earlier date, he is not believed about the past. But is his claim at least accepted from now on?
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים asked: if he spoke about the past, what is the law about believing him for the future?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question that builds on the answer just given. It is setting up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know a past claim fails and a future claim works. The question is about a mixed case. His words were about the past, so do we throw out his claim completely, or keep the part that applies from now on?

keyTerms.meaning: "It was asked of them." The חכמים raised an open question

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
If he spoke about the past,
what is the law about believing him for the future?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the past/future split from step 12 and asks about a case that falls in between.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a husband's claim of a past divorce, which is rejected for the past, is still accepted from now on.

steps.title: The core question: can one statement be split?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the general principle behind step 13's question: do we split one statement into an accepted part and a rejected part?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we split a statement, or do we not split a statement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the general idea behind the question from step 13. This sets up the disagreement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband said one thing: "I divorced her at an earlier date." We already know the past part is rejected. The question is whether we can still accept the part he has the power to do now, so that she counts as divorced from now on.

phrases.english: Do we divide the statement,
phrases.notes: Splitting means accepting the "from now on" part of his claim while rejecting the "earlier date" part.

phrases.english: or do we not divide the statement?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי פָּלְגִינַן דִּבּוּרָא, אוֹ לָא פָּלְגִינַן דִּבּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates step 13's specific question as a general principle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one statement can be partly accepted and partly rejected.

steps.title: רב מארי and רב זביד disagree
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים argue: one says we split the statement, and the other says we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מארי and רב זביד disagree. One says we split the statement, and the other says we do not split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a disagreement about the question from step 14. It does not tell us which אמורא holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we split, the woman is divorced from now on, because the husband has the power to divorce her now. If we do not split, his whole claim falls, because its past part cannot be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: one says (the speaker is not named)

phrases.english: Rav Mari and Rav Zevid [disagree];
One says: we divide,
and one says: we do not divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מָארִי וְרַב זְבִיד חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two possible answers to step 14's question as a dispute between אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether a husband's statement can be split.

steps.title: Challenge from רבא: we do split a husband's testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the "no splitting" view from רבא's ruling. A husband's testimony that a man committed adultery with his wife counts against the man but not against the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from רבא's ruling? רבא said that if a husband says, "So-and-so had relations with my wife," the husband and one more witness together can have that man put to death. That means the man can be killed, but not the wife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view that we never split a statement. It points to רבא, who clearly does split the husband's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's testimony describes a single act. רבא still accepts it against the man and rejects it against the wife, because a husband cannot testify about his own wife. So splitting a statement seems to be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: to kill him (have him put to death)

phrases.english: What is different from Rava's ruling?
For Rava said:
"So-and-so had relations with my wife" —
he and another witness combine to have him put to death.
To kill him, but not to kill her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the "we do not split" view in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that we do not split a statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא splits one statement: it is accepted against the man and rejected against the wife. So splitting should be possible here too.

steps.title: Two people can be split, one person cannot
steps.stepSummary: We split a statement when it involves two different people, but not when it involves only one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: With two bodies, we split the statement. With one body, we do not split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the "no splitting" view. It shows that רבא's case is different from the divorce case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case the testimony is about two people, the man and the wife, so it can be accepted for one and rejected for the other. In the divorce case the whole claim is about one woman, and her single status cannot be partly believed and partly rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: פלגינן דיבורא works when a statement involves two different people (תרי גופי), but according to this view not when it involves one person (חד גופא).

phrases.english: With regard to two bodies, we divide;
with regard to one body, we do not divide.
phrases.notes: In the divorce claim, everything is about one woman, so it can't be split.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּתְרֵי גוּפֵי פָּלְגִינַן, בְּחַד גּוּפָא לָא פָּלְגִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבא in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (two people versus one person).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's ruling seemed to show that any statement can be split.
steps.terutzMaskana: Splitting works only when the statement concerns two separate people. The divorce claim concerns one person, so the view that we do not split it still stands.
